title.rendered: Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026: Complete Festival Schedule, Rituals, Kodiyettam & Arattu  Details

content.rendered:
Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026 – Complete Festival Schedule, Rituals & Highlights

Guruvayur Ulsavam The famous annual festival of Guruvayur Temple, Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026, will be celebrated with immense devotion and traditional splendor from February 20 to March 9, 2026. The nine-day festival is one of the most important temple celebrations in Kerala, drawing thousands of devotees, artists, and visitors to Guruvayur.

The Guruvayur Ulsavam is one of the beautiful blends of sacred temple rituals, majestic elephant processions, traditional melam, classical art performances, and the spiritually significant Aarattu ceremony.

Kalavara Nirakkal – The Ritual Preparations (Feb 20 – Feb 27, 2026)

The celebrations started  with Kalavara Nirakkal, a traditional ritual marking the ceremonial preparation for the festival. During these days:

  • Special poojas are conducted.
  • Offerings are arranged in the temple store (Kalavara)
  • Devotees participate in sacred rituals.
  • Temple premises begin festive decorations.
  •  

These preparatory days build spiritual anticipation among devotees.

Kodiyettam – Official Beginning of Ulsavam (March 1, 2026)

In the Guruvayur Ulsavam the most awaited moment, Kodiyettam (flag hoisting), marks the official starting of Guruvayur Ulsavam. The ceremonial flag is hoisted in the temple premises amidst Vedic chants and devotional music.

From that moment, the temple atmosphere transforms into a vibrant spiritual festival ground.

Daily Rituals During Ulsavam

In Guruvayur Ulsavam, each day begins early morning with traditional temple rituals including:

  • Nirmalyam
  • Abhishekam
  • Usha Pooja
  • Pantheeradi Pooja
  • Seeveli (procession inside temple)

In Guruvayur Ulsavam, you can see the rhythmic beats of chenda and traditional instruments accompany the Seeveli, where beautiful elephants add grandeur to the ritual.

Evening rituals and deepa-alankaram create a mesmerizing devotional experience for devotees.

Cultural Programs & Artistic Celebrations

One of the biggest highlights in  Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026 is the wide variety of cultural programs organized every day.

Across the festival days, devotees can witness:

  • Classical dance performances like Bharatanatyam and Mohiniyattam
  • Kathakali performances
  • Carnatic music concerts
  • Devotional singing programs
  • Bhajans and Sopana Sangeetham
  • Instrumental concerts
  • Drama and traditional art presentations

Renowned artists, upcoming talents, and cultural groups participate in these programs, making the evenings lively and spiritually enriching.

Children’s performances and group dance presentations also add energy and enthusiasm to the festival.

Special Highlights (March 7 – March 9, 2026)

The final days of the Ulsavam are especially grand.

Ulsavam Day 8 (March 7 – Saturday)
  • Special Seeveli
  • Devotional performances
  • Evening cultural programs
  • Temple rituals with large devotee participation
Ulsavam Day 9 (March 8 – Sunday)
  • Extended temple rituals
  • Pallivetta (symbolic royal hunt ritual)
  • Cultural programs and devotional gatherings
Ulsavam Day 10 (March 9 – Monday) – Aarattu Day

The last days of festival includes with the sacred Aarattu ceremony, where the idol of Lord Guruvayurappan is ceremonially taken for the holy bath. This ritual symbolizes purification and the formal conclusion of the festival.

Devotees gather in huge numbers to witness Aarattu, considering it highly auspicious.

Elephant Procession & Melam

The presence of beautifully decorated elephants during Seeveli is one of the most iconic aspects of Guruvayur Ulsavam. The traditional melam featuring chenda, ilathalam, kombu, and kuzhal creates a divine and energetic atmosphere within the temple premises.

The synchronized rhythm of percussion instruments and the visual grandeur of elephants carrying the deity make the festival unforgettable.

Spiritual & Cultural Significance

Guruvayur Ulsavam is not just a temple festival—it is a celebration of faith, culture, and Kerala’s rich artistic heritage.

For devotees, it is a time to seek blessings of Lord Guruvayurappan.

For artists, it is a prestigious platform to perform.

For visitors, it is an opportunity to experience the true essence of Kerala’s temple traditions.

The entire town of Guruvayur comes alive during Ulsavam, filled with devotion, music, lamps, and festive energy.

Plan Your Visit

If you are planning to visit Guruvayur during Ulsavam 2026:

  • Arrive early for morning rituals
  • Expect heavy crowds during Kodiyettam and Aarattu
  • Attend evening cultural programs for a complete festival experience
  • Follow temple dress code and guidelines

Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026 promises nine days of devotion, tradition, and grand celebration. Whether you are a devotee or a lover of classical arts, this festival offers a spiritually uplifting and culturally rich experience.

Stay tuned to Guruvayur Live for daily updates and detailed schedules of Guruvayur Ulsavam 2026.

title.rendered: Guruvayur Temple Entry Rules & Regulations (Dos & Don’ts 2026 Guide)

content.rendered:
Guruvayur Temple entry rules – Introduction

The Guruvayur Temple, which  dedicated to Lord Krishna as Guruvayurappan, is not just a place of worship god — also it’s a spiritual center built on centuries of faith and discipline.

In this temple every visitor, whether they are from local or they are from abroad, is expected to follow a set of rules and customs which preserve the temple’s sanctity.

All Devotees should understand these dos and dont’s  and it will help you experience a smooth, respectful, and spiritually fulfilling darshan.

·      

Guruvayur Temple entry rules

All the Devotees should follow certain rules in Guruvayur Temple. What are those

Dress Code for men women and children

Entry area and Queue Discipline

Photography,  Mobile Phones and Reels Shooting

Footwear, smart watches & other Belongings

Cleanliness & Purity Rules

Restrictions on Entry

Offerings & Donations

Behavior & Silence

Let’s Go through all these deeply
 1. Dress Code for Men & Women in Guruvayur temple

All devotee must wear traditional attire (as per temple dress code):

  • Men have to wear Mundu (white dhoti), no shirts or pants inside the temple.
  • Women have to wear Saree, set mundu, or salwar kameez — no jeans, leggings, or western wear.
    Those not dressed appropriately may be denied entry.
2. Entry Points and Queue Discipline in Guruvayur temple

There are 3 main entries

  • Main entry through East Nada (Eastern Gate).
  • Maintain silence in the queue — no overtaking or pushing.
  • Follow the instructions of temple volunteers and Devaswom staff.
  • Entry is permitted only through designated queue systems.
3. Photography, Mobile Phones and Reels Shooting in Guruvayur temple
  • Cameras and mobile phones are strictly prohibited inside the temple premises.
  • You must keep all the electronic devices into the official counters near the entrance before entry.
  • Taking selfies, shooting reels or videos near the sanctum is considered disrespectful and it’s banned from high court order.
4. Footwear, Smart watches & Other Belongings in Guruvayur temple
  • Footwear is not allowed beyond the temple gates. You need to keep the designated chappal into designated area.
  • Devotee should avoid carrying large bags, handbags, or leather items inside.
  • If you’re carrying any kind offerings (nivedyam) also you should ensure they’re purchased from temple-authorized counters.
5. Cleanliness & Purity Rules in Guruvayur temple
  • Devotees should take a bath before entering the temple and should wear a proper cleaned dress — cleanliness is a sacred discipline here.
  • Devotees should avoid chewing gum, eating, or drinking inside the temple complex.
  • Drinking Alcohol, smoking, and non-vegetarian food are strictly banned nearby premises of the temple.
6. Restrictions on Entry into the Guruvayur Temple

As per temple customs:

  • In Guruvayur Temple only Hindus are permitted entry inside the sanctum.
  • Non-Hindus can visit the surroundings but not the inner sanctum.
  • Devotees under the influence of alcohol or wearing improper attire are not allowed.
 7. Offerings & Donations in Guruvayur temple
  • Devotees should do all offerings through official counters of Guruvayur Devaswom.
  • You can donate through via official receipts or the online portal.
  • You should avoid giving money or offerings to unauthorized individuals.
8. Behaviour & Silence in Guruvayur temple
  • Devotee’s should maintain silence and discipline inside the temple.
  • Please avoid unnecessary conversations or loud chanting.
  • You should avoid touch the deity, the sanctum door, or temple ornaments.
  • Sit quietly in meditation or chant softly while waiting for darshan.
  •  

Don’ts in Guruvayur Temple entry rules

Dos for a Peaceful Visit in Guruvayur Temple

  • devotee should reach early, especially for morning darshan.
  • you should deposit your belongings in the counters before entry.
  • please carry small change for offerings and prasadam.
  • devotees can visit nearby sub-temples (Ganapathy, Devi, Sastha) before entering the main shrine.
  • Everyone should respect senior citizens, children, and differently-abled devotees in queue.

Conclusion

All devotees should follow the rules and customs of Guruvayur Temple, it’s not just about discipline — they’re about devotion, humility, and respect for Lord Guruvayurappan.

By following the small things you can enjoy a peaceful and memorable  visits to the Guruvayur temple

title.rendered: Guruvayur Temple: Top 3 Travel Tips & Darshan Timings Every Devotee Should Know

content.rendered:
History of Guruvayur Temple

The Guruvayur temple is considered an ancient Hindu temple and the major pilgrimage center in Kerala. It is also known as the “Dwaraka of the south”.

The supreme deity of the Guruvayur temple is lord Krishna, worshipped in the Bala Krishna form that represents innocence and divinity. It is believed that the idol of lord Krishna is around 5000 years old.

Based on Hindu mythology, the temple was consecrated by the deva guru, Brihaspathi, and the vayu ( wind god).

The Guruvayur temple is one of the important pilgrimage sites of Kerala, and it is called the Dwaraka of the south. The ruler of Calicut, known as Zamorins, played a fabulous role in the development of the Guruvayur temple, and it made the temple more popular among the devotees.

The temple faced a lot of adversities, including the invasion of Dutch rulers and Tipu Sultan during the 14th and 18th centuries, and the temple lost everything in a fire. But the idol of lord Krishna and the other deities were still preserved by the devotees, and it was reinstalled.

In 1970, the temple was again destroyed due to fire, and the collective efforts of the devotees helped in the reconstruction of the temple with more pride.

The temple was not accessible to the devotees who belonged to the lower castes, so during the 20th century, massive protests were conducted under the guidance of K. Kelappan, who is known as the Kerala Gandhi. This helped the devotees to enter the temple irrespective of caste.

The temple also witnessed lots of adversities, historical events, and miracles. This led the temple to become more popular and made it a must-visit place for Hindus to seek spiritual happiness.

 

Guruvayur Temple Timings
  • Morning rituals

Nimalyam – 3.00 am to 3.30 am

Malar nivedyam and alankaram – 3.30 am to 4.15 am

Ethirettu pooja – 4.30 am to 6.15 am

  • Midday rituals

Ucha pooja – 11.30 am to 12.30 pm

  • The temple remains closed from 1.30 pm to 4.30 pm
  • Evening rituals

Deeparadhana – 6.00 pm to 6.45 pm

Athazha pooja nivedyam – 7.30 pm to 7.45 pm

Athazha Seeveli – 8.45 pm to 9.00 pm

  • Closing time – 9.15 pm
TEMPLE ACCESSIBILITY
  • The temple is situated in the town of Guruvayur, in the Thrissur district of Kerala
  • The nearest airport is Cochin International Airport
  • The nearest railway station is Guruvayur railway station, and the Thrissur railway station
  • Direct bus services are available from the major cities
TEMPLE ADDRESS

         Guruvayur Sri Krishna temple, Guruvayur, Thrissur district, Kerala – 680101, India

TEMPLE CONTACT DETAILS
  • Phone – +914872556335
  • Official website – Guruvayur Devaswom

content.rendered:
Guruvayur temple is one of the most famous and popular ancient Hindu temples in Kerala. It is located at Guruvayur in the Thrissur district. The temple is mainly dedicated to the lord Krishna, known as Guruvayoorappan. In Guruvayur Temple, you can see the idol of Guruvayoorappan in the four-armed form of lord Vishnu. The temple is also known as the Dwaraka of the South, which attracts millions of devotees from different parts of the world.

The Guruvayur temple is considered one of the 108 abhimana kshetras in the Vyshnava tradition. The idol of the guruvayoorappan is unique and it is known as guruvayur Unnikrishnan (unni Kannan). It represents the image of lord Krishna in his childhood form standing with four arms. This form is also called chathurbhahu or Vishnu Maya. 

There are many specialties you can find in Guruvayur temple. The idol is made up of a different kind of black stone called “Patala Anjanam” which has divine properties. Even the idol of deity Guruvayoorappan represents some importance. The four different hands of the guruvayoorappan carry different items such as “Shankha”, “Sudarshana chakra”, “Gada”, and “Padma”.

The “Conch” or “Shankha” is held in the upper left hand, which represents the sound of “OM”, it is believed to as the source of all creations. “Sudharshana Chakra” is carried on the upper right hand and it is thought to as the most powerful weapon used to protect the right in the universe. “Lotus”, also called “Padma” is held in the lower left hand and represents purity and divine wisdom. The “Mace” which is named the “Kaumodaki gada” held in the lower right hand represents the supreme power of the deity to destroy evil forces.

The Guruvayur temple has a significant role in Hindu mythology and its history is related to the ancient legends and the divine legends.

As per Hindu mythology, the idol of the lord Guruvayur Unnikrishnan was originally worshipped by the lord Vishnu in vaikunta and later it was passed to the lord “Brahma”. Further, the idol was given to the devout couple Sutapas (̌ “Prajapati Sutapa” ) and “Prsni” ( “Devaki” in one of her early births). Through their intense worship and devotion , the lord Vishnu granted them a boon. The lord Vishnu itself would be born as the son of these devout couples in three different lives. Later, sutapas and prsni were blessed with the prsnigarbha in the first birth and in the second birth the ” Sutapas ” and “Prsni” were born as kashyapa and ” Aditi “, parents of ” Vamana “. 

They were born as “Vasudeva” and “Devaki”, parents of lord ” Krishna” in their third life. In all their life the lord ” Guruvayoorappan ” idol was worshipped by the parents with great devotion. ” Krishna ” was the last form of the lord ” Vishnu ” in earthly life, so when it came to an end the “Krishna” wanted the idol to be preserved and he instructed to one of his devotees named “Udhava” to preserve the idol in a safe location. The “Udhava” followed the instructions of the lord “Krishna” and he traveled to many places looking for the proper place to keep the the idol. With the help of the Guru (“Brihaspathy” who is considered the guru of gods) and the “Vayu” (the wind god), the “Udhava” reached a peaceful place where the lord “Shiva” and “Parvati” were worshipping. So to provide enough space for the idol the lord “Shiva” and “Parvati” graciously moved to the nearest place which is called “Mammiyoor”. Hence the place where the idol of lord “Krishna” was fixed later came to be known as the “Guruvayur”, which is a combination of guru and vayu.

Kururamma is known for her strong devotion to the lord “Krishna” and it is also intertwined with the history of the Guruvayur temple. “Kururamma” was a childless widow who adopted lord “Krishna”, Guruvayoorappan as her child. She was born in a village named Parur which was “Gauri” and she was the last woman of the “Kurur illam”.

Guruvayoor Keshavan was one of the most famous temple elephants in India. He was caught from the Nilambur forest and adopted by the Nilamboor royal family as their 12th elephant. Keshavan was the tallest elephant that lived in Kerala and he was about 3.28 metre tall. The king of the nilamboor royal family prayed to guruvayoorappan to save his familiesfrom enemies and he offered one of his elephant to the temple if his wish was fulfilled. As he promised the king given the elephant Keshava to the guruvayoor temple on 4 January 1922. Later the Guruvayoor Devaswam board gave him the title Gajarajan which means the king of elephants. Guruvayoor keshavan would bend his legs only in front of those who were carrying the lord Thidambu and all others had to climb through his hind legs. During the time of Guruvayur Ekadeshi in 1976, Keshavan became sick and he died after few days on 2nd December 1976. The Guruvayoor Devaswam board celebrates the anniversary of his death on the evening of every Ekadashi by lining up all the elephants in front of the statue of the Guruvayur Keshavan as a tribute to him.
